profile.facility_type_note: JFK12 and JFK13 are two of the most historically significant carrier hotel buildings in the world. JFK12 is at 60 Hudson Street, Manhattan, built in 1930 as the Western Union Building, now one of the most important internet peering and interconnection points on the US East Coast. JFK13 is at 32 Avenue of the Americas, built in 1932 as AT&T's Long Distance headquarters, also a major carrier hotel. Both addresses confirmed via Digital Realty's own site.

reading.body:
JFK13 is a historic carrier hotel in Manhattan built in 1932 as AT&T's Long Distance headquarters, now operated by Digital Realty at 32 Avenue of the Americas. The facility's critical IT load capacity is not confirmed from a tier-1 source, and the operator's own specification pages value this building primarily for interconnection density rather than raw megawattage. This positioning reflects the site's role in the legacy carrier and peering infrastructure of the US East Coast rather than its function in modern compute-intensive AI workloads.

Among New York state's 31 mapped data center facilities, only one operator has published IT megawatt capacity figures. JFK13 ranks second in the state by published capacity, though the state context itself—with just 3 MW published across all facilities—shows that New York's data center footprint remains opaque to public specification. Without disclosed IT load, the campus's potential to host GPU clusters or AI infrastructure cannot be read from available facts.

The historical significance of this address in US telecommunications and internet routing does not translate to published specifications about its current power delivery, cooling, or physical density. Whether JFK13 has been architecturally adapted to support modern AI training hardware, or remains primarily a colocation and peering point for network traffic, is not stated in the operator's published specifications.
